chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Nājiyah, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): “Al-Mughīrah says that the believer is not afflicted with leprosy, nor with vitiligo, nor with such-and-such, nor with such-and-such.”

So he said: “Then he is surely heedless of the Companion of Yā Sīn; he was crippled in the hand.” Then he drew back his fingers and said: “It is as though I am looking at his crippling. He came to them and warned them, then he returned to them on the following day, and they killed him.”
Then he said: “Indeed, the believer may be afflicted with every affliction and may die by every kind of death, except that he does not kill himself.”

key_terms.الْبَرَصِ: vitiligo or a depigmenting skin disease; another example of affliction
key_terms.الْجُذَامِ: leprosy; cited as an example of severe bodily affliction
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer; the faithful person whose trials are being discussed
key_terms.بَلِيَّةٍ: affliction, trial, or calamity that befalls a person
key_terms.مُكَنَّعًا: crippled or with a withered/contracted hand
key_terms.مِيتَةٍ: a manner or kind of death

ai.seo_question: Can a believer be afflicted with severe illness or die in painful ways according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects the claim that a believer is exempt from severe bodily afflictions such as leprosy or vitiligo. Imam Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) cites the Companion of Yā Sīn as an example that a faithful person may suffer bodily impairment and even be killed, while affirming that the believer may face every trial except self-killing.
